items.title: Williams, Aston Martin among new F1 liveries for Las Vegas GP as Acura "replaces" Honda
items.summary: Williams and Aston Martin are among the F1 teams to have revamped their car liveries for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix. F1 heads to Las Vegas for its third of three US races, with the entertainment capital having quickly become one of the series' key commercial weekends for teams and their partners.

items.title: Lando Norris's LN4 Fusion signs former Red Bull junior Oliver Goethe as its first F2 driver
items.summary: Lando Norris's new junior team LN4 Fusion has signed former Red Bull junior Oliver Goethe as its first driver for the 2027 Formula 2 season. The 22-year-old will make the move from MP Motorsport for his third season in F2, after celebrating two podium finishes so far this year.

items.title: Lando Norris: F1 needs better rain tyres as wet Las Vegas would be "scary"
items.summary: World champion Lando Norris hopes Formula 1 tyre supplier Pirelli will field much-improved rain tyres in 2027 as he expects the current range won't work properly at a low-downforce circuit like Las Vegas.

items.title: Toto Wolff predicts Kimi Antonelli will become more popular in Italy than Michael Schumacher
items.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff is no stranger to making bold statements, but his latest assessment of Kimi Antonelli's popularity might actually shock the dedicated Ferrari fanbase. Following Antonelli's historic 2026 drivers' championship victory in Mexico City, Wolff sat down for an exclusive interview with the German publication BILD.

items.title: Zak Brown recalls McLaren's "very toxic environment" after joining team in 2016
items.summary: McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown has described the team he joined in 2016 as "a very toxic environment", blaming a revolving door of leaders for years of poor results on and off the track.

items.title: Lewis Hamilon reportedly house-hunting in LA amid Kim Kardashian relationship
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton wants a Los Angeles base so he can spend more of the winter break with his partner Kim Kardashian and her children, according to a report from the Daily Mail. The report says the Ferrari driver approached estate agents about houses in Malibu, Pacific Palisades and the Hollywood Hills, and is weighing up whether to rent or buy.

items.title: F1 Las Vegas GP 2026: start time, schedule and how to watch
items.summary: The Las Vegas Grand Prix starts at 8 pm PT on Saturday, November 21, which is 11 pm ET. The race runs at night along the Strip, and every session is live on Apple TV. Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 schedule Session Day PT MT CT ET Practice 1 Thursday, Nov. 19 4:30 pm 5:30 pm 6:30 pm 7:30 pm Practice 2 Thursday, Nov.

items.title: F1 Las Vegas GP 2026: UK times, schedule and how to watch
items.summary: The Las Vegas Grand Prix starts at 4am UK time on Sunday 22 November. In Las Vegas it is still 8pm on Saturday, because the race runs at night along the Strip. Every session falls overnight in the UK, and every one of them is live on Sky Sports F1.

items.title: F1 driver manager Enrico Zanarini recounts his 50 years in motorsport
items.summary: Sometimes, a single incident – mere seconds – is enough to alter the course of a career. Enrico Zanarini recalls one such moment, which took place in the paddock at the 1993 Portuguese Grand Prix. Emanuele Naspetti, one of the drivers Zanarini managed in the early 1990s, was striving to secure his Formula 1 future.

items.title: Christian Horner reveals how Max Verstappen’s management reshaped 2022 Red Bull development
items.summary: The narrative surrounding Sergio Perez's tenure at Red Bull Racing often centres on his inability to consistently extract the same raw pace as his team-mate Max Verstappen. But former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner recently pulled back the curtain on a behind-the-scenes engineering battle that altered the trajectory of Perez's 2022 season.

items.title: James Allison reveals message to Mercedes recruits during team's four-year F1 title drought
items.summary: Mercedes technical director James Allison has revealed how he told hundreds of staff members who joined the Brackley outfit during the team's lean years that they would one day win, and that the championship would be theirs.

items.title: Haas sticks with Rafael Camara for Las Vegas, Ryo Hirakawa in for FP1
items.summary: Rafael Camara will race again for Haas at Formula 1's upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix, as Ryo Hirakawa takes Ollie Bearman's seat for the opening practice session. Both Hirakawa and Camara have now raced for the team following the dismissal of Esteban Ocon, who was stood down during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend.

items.title: What is left to fight for in F1 2026?
items.summary: A five-way battle for P2 in the drivers’ championship Kimi Antonelli romped to his maiden world title to become Formula 1’s youngest world champion, but behind him it’s all to play for – and closer than ever.

items.title: Christian Horner admits Red Bull prospects were thrown in against Max Verstappen too soon
items.summary: The second seat at Red Bull Racing has long been viewed as one of the most high-pressure environments in Formula 1. While the Milton Keynes operation frequently cycled through highly rated prospects trying to find a match for Max Verstappen, former team principal Christian Horner is now openly questioning the logic of that ruthless driver pipeline.

items.title: Topps reveals Gem Mint 10 Lando Norris card with Coca-Cola suit patch
items.summary: Topps has shared one of its rarest Lando Norris cards: a signed 2024 Dynasty Formula 1 card with two pieces of race suit, one of them cut from the Coca-Cola logo on the sleeve of his McLaren race suit.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton criticises ex-F1 drivers for "talking smack" about young stars
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton has criticised former drivers for "talking smack" about the young stars of the series, saying he has always been determined not to become "that type of driver". The Briton was asked at Interlagos whether Kimi Antonelli's title success had made him reflect on his own career.

items.title: Christian Horner explains why Max Verstappen’s “abnormal” driving style destroys his team-mates
items.summary: The narrative surrounding Red Bull Racing over the last half-decade has consistently featured a rotating cast of drivers struggling - and often failing - to survive alongside Max Verstappen. Former team principal Christian Horner recently provided a technical explanation for the phenomenon.

items.title: Retaining Liam Lawson isn't enough – Red Bull must stop treating him like a failure
items.summary: Liam Lawson never failed at Red Bull Racing in 2025. It was Red Bull that failed Liam Lawson. Retaining his services for another year isn't just a logical decision, but perhaps the first sign that the organisation is changing the habits it developed under Helmut Marko. Yet there may be one more step it needs to take to avoid failing Lawson again.

items.title: Christian Horner blames Red Bull leadership structure for missing F1’s future stars
items.summary: For years, Red Bull Racing's dual-leadership structure between team principal Christian Horner and motorsport advisor Dr. Helmut Marko was praised as a ruthless but highly effective system. But Horner is now pointing to that exact management style as the primary reason the Milton Keynes squad lost out on Lando Norris, George Russell, and Oscar Piastri.

items.title: Mercedes pitwall admits floundering Ferraris relieved title pressure in São Paulo
items.summary: When the rain falls at Interlagos, chaos usually follows. For Mercedes, the 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix was a turbulent affair. The Brackley-based squad arrived in Brazil needing to execute a clean race to officially wrap up the constructors' championship, but quickly found themselves battling a highly unpredictable wet-dry track.

items.title: How Istanbul is revamping its F1 circuit to clinch long-term future
items.summary: Finding the right balance is often a challenge in modern Formula 1. That applies to the technical regulations: striking a balance between satisfying drivers and purists on the one hand, and delivering the spectacle F1 wants to offer younger fans on the other, with a constant stream of overtaking moves for, let’s say, the TikTok generation.

items.title: Mercedes technical director details the psychological toll of F1 underperformance
items.summary: In Formula 1, PR-trained executives routinely frame losing seasons as "learning opportunities" and promise that the team will quickly bounce back. But Mercedes technical director James Allison recently stripped away that polished narrative to reveal the psychological reality of a championship drought.

items.title: James Allison admits flawed “Update 18” made the Mercedes W17 a “handful”
items.summary: Mercedes stormed out of the gates in 2026, quickly establishing a dominant lead that ultimately secured both the drivers' and constructors' championships. But as the season nears its conclusion, the performance gap between the W17 and the rest of the grid has visibly shrunk.

items.title: Oscar Piastri: You've got to "manhandle" McLaren's F1 car to find its potential
items.summary: Oscar Piastri says McLaren's 2026 Formula 1 car has to be "manhandled" to be quick, describing the MCL40 as a car that punishes drivers the moment they are not at the limit. The Australian driver has endured a difficult campaign after fighting for the title last year. He has two podiums in Japan and Miami, and sits seventh in the drivers' standings with three races to go.

items.title: ‘Lewis suspected a conspiracy’ – Nico Rosberg explains how Lewis Hamilton F1 rivalry went awry at Mercedes
items.summary: When Lewis Hamilton joined Nico Rosberg at Mercedes for the 2013 Formula 1 season, it was a feel-good story: two long-time friends becoming team-mates. However, their amicable relationship soon turned sour, as Mercedes dominated the world championship’s early turbo hybrid era from 2014 and title battles turned into intra-team duels.

items.title: Topps celebrates Lewis Hamilton’s 400th F1 start with limited NOW card
items.summary: Topps has released a Topps NOW trading card in celebration of Lewis Hamilton's 400th Formula 1 start, which came at the São Paulo Grand Prix last weekend. The Ferrari driver became only the second driver in the championship's history to reach the milestone, after Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso, who got there in 2024.

items.title: Mercedes and Audi unveil adidas collections for F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
items.summary: Mercedes and Audi have unveiled special adidas fan collections for the upcoming Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Mercedes' range is called "Neon Lights", while Audi's is named "After Hours". Both collections are available now through adidas.com, and the pieces listed on the brand's US store range in price from $30 to $200. The most expensive items are the outerwear.

items.title: Max Verstappen signs ambassador deal with Dutch technical group VDK
items.summary: Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has become the new ambassador of the VDK Group, a Dutch group of installation and technical companies that is expanding across Europe. The Dutchman will play a prominent role in the company's international branding over the coming years and will feature in its communications and marketing campaigns.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli meets Italian president Sergio Mattarella
items.summary: "To President Mattarella, with great admiration," signed Kimi Antonelli. The new Formula 1 world champion is in the middle of a whirlwind of meetings, events and celebrations for the world title he won two weeks ago at the Mexico Grand Prix, with which he ended a title drought for an Italian driver to win the world championship dating back to 1953.

items.title: McLaren to upgrade MCL40 car at its bogey F1 track Las Vegas
items.summary: McLaren will introduce upgrades to its MCL40 at Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the new parts labelled as “the foundation for next year’s car”.
